title: P0-binary control re-run evidence (M6.2)
note: Archived evidence for the P0-JVM control re-run cited in kffi/benchmarks/results/2026-08-16-f6cdb8f0-jvm-baseline.md (Run configuration section and Comparability note). Values are log-cited from the implementer's run on 2026-08-16 — they were not parsed from a JMH result.json, so no raw data, percentiles, or error bars are available. They are reproduced here so the ~4 ns (vs ~26 ns P0 absolutes) claim is independently checkable.

context.jmh_config: Mode.AverageTime, ns/op, 1 thread, warmup 3 x 1s, measurement 5 x 1s, forks 2 — identical to the P0 run (2026-08-12-012b50e9)
context.benchmark_binary: identical benchmark binary and configuration as the P0 run (kffi-benchmark-jvm, per-benchmark metadata verified against 2026-08-12-012b50e9-jvm-baseline.json)

runs.jvm: Temurin 25.0.3 (exact P0 JVM binary, via sdkman)
runs.purpose: Control: re-run the identical P0 benchmark binary and configuration on the exact P0 JVM binary to check whether the P0 ~26-27 ns absolutes reproduce; they did not (machine-state inflation on 2026-08-12), see Comparability note in the report.

runs.jvm: Temurin 25.0.1 (sdkman default, the P2 run JVM)
runs.purpose: Focused reproducibility check of the P2 full-suite run on the default JVM.

conclusion: Both re-runs reproduce ~4 ns for the byte-identical floor benchmarks, not the P0 ~26-27 ns absolutes; the P0 absolutes were inflated by machine state (concurrent Gradle/Kotlin-Native builds during M1-M5), not by code or JVM changes.
